title: PyTorch 2.15 Makes Rewritten NCCL Default, Adds FP8 on Apple Silicon
dek: Faster multi-GPU training plus quicker local decoding on Blackwell and Mac.

facts.label: Faster single-row softmax on Apple GPUs

caption:
The framework behind most of today's AI just got a quiet but major upgrade. ⚡

PyTorch 2.15 is out, and a rewritten NCCL backend now powers every multi-GPU job on NVIDIA hardware by default. A new flight recorder dumps a post-mortem from every GPU when training hangs, so engineers can finally see what froze a run. Teams can roll back with the nccl-legacy backend if needed.

The release also speeds up 4-bit NVFP4 decoding on NVIDIA Blackwell, brings FP8 support and faster mixture-of-experts decoding to Apple Silicon, and widens AMD (MI450, ROCm 10.0) and Intel GPU support. Heads up: Python 3.10 is dropped, so you'll need 3.11 or newer.

We're tracking it at AI Parabellum because cheaper, more reliable training and faster local models on a Mac affect nearly every AI app you use.

Running open models on a Mac? PyTorch 2.15 adds FP8, a 1.32x boost for mixture-of-experts decoding on M3 Ultra, and a public torch.mps.Stream API.

On the NVIDIA side, the rewritten NCCL backend is now the default for multi-GPU training, with a new flight recorder to debug stuck runs. 🛠️
